stem: A level is set up between a benchmark at elevation 100.00 m and a new point. The backsight reading on the benchmark is 1.52 m and the foresight reading on the new point is 2.31 m. What is the elevation of the new point?
eli5: The level gives you a flat line of sight. Add the rod reading at the known point to find how high that line is, then subtract the rod reading at the new point.
solution:
Height of instrument = 100.00 + 1.52 = 101.52 m.

New elevation = 101.52 - 2.31 = 99.21 m.

A bigger rod reading means lower ground.

stem: A four-sided parcel has corners, in order, at (0, 0), (60, 0), (80, 40) and (20, 50), with coordinates in metres. What is its area?
eli5: Walk around the corners in order. For each side, cross-multiply the coordinates, keep a running total, and halve it at the end.

stem: Two road cross-sections 20 m apart have cut areas of 24 m^{2} and 36 m^{2}. Using the average end area method, what is the volume of cut between them?
eli5: Picture a loaf of bread. Average the size of the two end slices and multiply by the length of the loaf.

stem: Place each azimuth, measured clockwise from north, on its bearing.
eli5: An azimuth is one angle all the way around the compass from north. A bearing says which half you are in, north or south, then how far you turn toward east or west.
solution:
45° is in the northeast quarter: N 45° E.

135° is 45° short of south, on the east side: S 45° E.

225° is 45° past south, on the west side: S 45° W.

315° is 45° short of north, on the west side: N 45° W.

stem: A road rises from elevation 102.4 m to elevation 108.9 m over a horizontal distance of 260 m. What is the grade?
eli5: Grade is rise over run, written as a percent. A 2.5% grade climbs 2.5 m for every 100 m you travel along the map.

stem: A slope distance of 250.00 m is measured at a vertical angle of 12° above horizontal. What is the horizontal distance?
eli5: A tape laid up a hill measures more than the distance on the map. The map distance is the flat leg of the triangle.
solution: Horizontal distance = slope distance × cos(vertical angle) = 250.00 cos 12° = 244.54 m.

stem: What should the interior angles of a closed five-sided traverse add up to?
eli5: Any closed shape can be cut into triangles, and every triangle holds 180°.
solution:
Sum = (n - 2)(180°) = (5 - 2)(180°) = 540°.

The difference between this and the measured sum is the angular misclosure.

stem: Two sides of a triangular parcel are 80 m and 60 m long and meet at an angle of 30°. What is the area of the parcel?
eli5: A triangle is half of a slanted rectangle. The sine of the angle accounts for the slant.

stem: A borrow pit measures 20 m by 30 m in plan. Its average depth of cut is 2.5 m. What volume is excavated?
eli5: Volume is the footprint of the pit times how deep it is on average.
solution: V = plan area × average depth = 20(30)(2.5) = 1,500 m^{3}.

stem: A traverse line is 200.00 m long with an azimuth of 60°. What is its departure (east-west component)?
eli5: Every survey line can be split into how far it goes north and how far it goes east. Departure is the east part.
solution:
Departure = L sin(azimuth) = 200 sin 60° = 173.2 m east.

The latitude (north part) is 200 cos 60° = 100.0 m.

stem: Point A has a northing of 1,000.00 m and an easting of 500.00 m. Point B is 100.00 m from A on a bearing of S 30° E. What is the northing of B?
eli5: A bearing that starts with S means you are heading south, so the northing goes down.
solution:
Change in northing = -100 cos 30° = -86.6 m.

Northing of B = 1,000.00 - 86.6 = 913.4 m. The easting increases by 100 sin 30° = 50.0 m.
